title: Makassar / Ternate
hook: 1600 → 1900. Two fixed dots; compare the reconstruction's labels.

knows: two points can be located on a map
doesNotKnow: how this reconstruction classifies Makassar / Ternate in 1600 and 1900, and what that comparison cannot establish

misconception: A historical map's region labels directly establish exact borders, continuous control and the history of everyone inside.
objective: Compare the source's labels at two fixed points in 1600 and 1900; distinguish the observed map pattern from claims about its cause or legitimacy.

claims.text: Makassar area anchor: 119.43, -5.15 (0 km from the nominal location); Ternate area anchor: 127.493148, 0.903137 (17.8 km from the nominal location). Modern place names orient the fixed comparison points, not historical settlement names or exact city centres.
claims.source: tools/history-maps/cases.mjs: nominal WGS84 longitude/latitude points; generate.mjs areaAnchor prefers the nearest point covered by both snapshots within 75 km, without selecting for an answer. map.json records nominal and actual coordinates and the offset. A place name is not an ancient-settlement claim.

claims.text: The 1600 and 1900 stages are clipped Mercator paths from these GeoJSON snapshots, with all matched NAME labels retained: [[["Malaysian Islamic states"],["Malaysian Islamic states"]],[["Netherlands Indies"],["Netherlands Indies"]]]. Map key and SVG titles use these labels; NAME is not SUBJECTO.
claims.source: Ring directions normalised for d3 spherical exteriors/holes; coordinates and feature order retained. https://github.com/aourednik/historical-basemaps/blob/da7a4b735ecef70aebdc9c73e409d8a2500d50f3/geojson/world_1600.geojson (SHA-256 7285c07eeedfda9048de5354ea1744d327b07614085e9696c5802bb54c86849c); GeoJSON features [[9],[9]]; https://github.com/aourednik/historical-basemaps/blob/da7a4b735ecef70aebdc9c73e409d8a2500d50f3/geojson/world_1900.geojson (SHA-256 9c9221c851eaba4948e11b2a0b078e89239231f8c74df0dc321750ae234f10b5); GeoJSON features [[31],[31]]

claims.text: At the two points, 1600 has same label and 1900 has same label. This supports the prediction answer and first reveal sentence.
claims.source: tools/history-maps/generate.mjs: geoContains on every feature; sorted unique NAME sets, exact set equality; missing sets stay unlabelled. https://github.com/aourednik/historical-basemaps/blob/da7a4b735ecef70aebdc9c73e409d8a2500d50f3/geojson/world_1600.geojson (SHA-256 7285c07eeedfda9048de5354ea1744d327b07614085e9696c5802bb54c86849c); GeoJSON features [[9],[9]]; https://github.com/aourednik/historical-basemaps/blob/da7a4b735ecef70aebdc9c73e409d8a2500d50f3/geojson/world_1900.geojson (SHA-256 9c9221c851eaba4948e11b2a0b078e89239231f8c74df0dc321750ae234f10b5); GeoJSON features [[31],[31]]

claims.text: The maps are approximate reconstructions. Two snapshots do not date a transition, establish continuity, explain causes, or settle present-day claims; an unlabelled dot does not prove empty land.
claims.source: https://github.com/aourednik/historical-basemaps/blob/da7a4b735ecef70aebdc9c73e409d8a2500d50f3/README.md, sections Conceptual limitations and disputed territories / Polygons; two-endpoint inference limit. Stage caption, reveal, hook 'reconstruction', and prediction wording are covered here. Cultural and research reviews remain required.

claims.text: Two reconstructed areas overlap at one point. How should an explorer report that? Answer: Keep both labels and expose the overlap Keeping all matching labels preserves the source's ambiguity. A draw order is not a historical verdict.
claims.source: https://github.com/aourednik/historical-basemaps/blob/da7a4b735ecef70aebdc9c73e409d8a2500d50f3/README.md (source limitations); tools/history-maps/generate.mjs recalls[6]. Interpret the dataset fields and projection, not historical causes.

recall.question: Two reconstructed areas overlap at one point. How should an explorer report that?
options: Keep both labels and expose the overlap
recall.why: Keeping all matching labels preserves the source's ambiguity. A draw order is not a historical verdict.

careLine: Source NAME labels are classifications, not statements of legitimate sovereignty, ethnicity, religion, language or absence of people. Modern place names are orientation aids only. Retain missing coverage and overlapping labels.
